findings.title: No single owner of transfer state — the transfer state machine is scattered across 4 processes with no coordinator
findings.detail: A single player transfer is driven by ad-hoc handlers spread across: source shard trigger (ship-shard hull_exit_check, planet ship-reentry/EVA-board triggers), the system-shard acting as BOTH router (ship<->planet relay) AND owner (EVA/warp/boarding spawn), the destination shard (process_handoffs + observer-promote), and the client controller (network.rs ShardHandoff/ShardRedirect + registry.rs grace/promote). No component holds the authoritative transfer state or sequences the steps; each side reacts to messages and mutates local maps (pending_handoffs, PendingPlayerHandoffs.outgoing/incoming, boarding_pending, session_observers, secondaries, GraceWindow, SpawnPoseLatch, PendingSecondaryConnects). This is the root architectural reason transfers are hard to fix: there is no place to add a timeout, a retry, or a rollback because no one owns the lifecycle. ARCHITECTURAL FLAW.

findings.title: HandoffPending is inserted but NEVER removed — any un-acked handoff permanently freezes the player with no timeout/rollback
findings.detail: All four source triggers insert the HandoffPending marker component to make the trigger idempotent, but a repo-wide grep for any removal (remove::<HandoffPending>) returns ZERO matches. The marker only clears when the entity is despawned, which only happens inside process_handoff_accepted on a successful HandoffAccepted. If the destination never acks — QUIC packet dropped, peer_registry address miss, destination shard crash mid-transfer, or the destination shard not yet provisioned — the source player entity is permanently excluded (the queries filter Without<HandoffPending>) from hull_exit, physics, and input, AND the client is never sent a ShardHandoff/ShardRedirect. There is no timeout, retry, or rollback path anywhere in the codebase. The pending maps (pending_handoffs, PendingPlayerHandoffs, boarding_pending, session_observers) likewise have no TTL. This is the single highest-leverage cause of 'transfers that don't work and can't be fixed.' ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (the design has no failure handling).
findings.evidence: grep remove::<HandoffPending> => 0 hits; inserts at ship-shard/src/main.rs:2538,2617, planet-shard/src/main.rs:2745, system-shard/src/main.rs:5372; consumed-only-on-success: ship-shard/src/main.rs:1232-1237, planet-shard/src/main.rs:1860-1875

findings.title: Eviction landmine: client secondary FIFO eviction is actually arbitrary (HashMap order) and can drop the very secondary about to be promoted
findings.detail: MAX_SECONDARIES=4 caps non-scene (Ship/Planet) secondaries. When a new ShardPreConnect would exceed the cap, handle_preconnect evicts via secondaries.keys().find(|st| !is_scene_context(*st)) — but secondaries is a std HashMap, so iteration order is non-deterministic; the doc comment claims 'oldest/FIFO' (network.rs:41,656) but the code evicts an ARBITRARY entry. If the player is near several ships/planets (>4) and a ShardPreConnect arrives, the destination-to-be secondary can be evicted right before its ShardHandoff lands. Then ShardHandoff finds dest_key absent and falls back to the fresh-handshake path (network.rs:472-499), defeating seamless promotion and churning connections — exactly the prompt's 'eviction landmine where cross-shard visibility breaks because observer entries get evicted.' Compounded by the source shard replying observer_promoted=true based on has_session_observer at the DESTINATION while the CLIENT may have already evicted its half — the two sides disagree about whether the observer exists. ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (LRU/pinning semantics absent; promote target not pinned).
findings.evidence: client/src/net/network.rs:190-193,692-717 (evict loop using keys().find), 410-499 (ShardHandoff fallback); cap doc at network.rs:40-44

findings.title: Source shard despawns the player IMMEDIATELY on HandoffAccepted — no ghost/demote grace despite source_demote_after_ticks existing in the protocol
findings.detail: The protocol defines source_demote_after_ticks (default 15 ≈ 750 ms) and GhostUpdate specifically so the source keeps the player as a ghost until the destination's first authoritative tick reaches all observers. But the actual source handlers despawn the player entity and unregister the client synchronously the moment HandoffAccepted arrives: ship-shard despawns at line 1232-1237 and unregisters at 1223-1224; planet despawns at 1860-1875 and unregisters at 1853-1854. No GhostUpdate is ever sent (grep shows GhostUpdate is defined in core/handoff.rs and the fbs but emitted nowhere). So other players watching the source see the departing player pop out of existence for the inter-shard + client-handshake window. The grace machinery that DOES exist is only client-side (transition.rs GraceWindow for the leaving player's own chunk view), not for third-party observer continuity. IMPLEMENTATION GAP that the protocol was designed to cover but never wired.
findings.evidence: ship-shard/src/main.rs:1216-1237; planet-shard/src/main.rs:1846-1875; protocol intent in core/src/handoff.rs:134-228 (GhostUpdate, source_demote_after_ticks doc); shard-common/src/handoff_pipeline.rs:15-21; GhostUpdate emit sites: none

findings.title: Hull trap mitigation (enforce_ship_exit_clearance) is best-effort and races the cross-shard hull sync — it silently gives up
findings.detail: On ship->planet disembark the player can be trapped inside their own landed ship hull. The fix (planet-shard/src/main.rs:1548-1621) pushes the player out the nearest horizontal hull face, but it requires three independent async streams to have arrived first: the NearbyShip pose (process_ship_nearby), the NearbyShipHull bounds (process_ship_colliders), AND an initialized SurfaceAnchor (set at first player spawn). If the hull hasn't synced within the ShipExitClearance.until_tick safety window, the marker is removed and the player is left wherever they are — possibly still inside the hull (lines 1564-1569, 1617-1619). The spawn position itself also depends on whether NearbyShip is tracked yet (process_handoffs:1243-1288), with a 1km altitude clamp band-aid for the race where it isn't. The hull trap is therefore an emergent multi-stream ordering race, not a local bug. ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (depenetration depends on eventual cross-shard convergence with a hard timeout that just abandons the correction).
findings.evidence: planet-shard/src/main.rs:1502-1536 (clear_player_of_hull), 1548-1621 (enforce_ship_exit_clearance, safety expiry 1564-1569), 1216-1288 (spawn racing NearbyShip), 1656-1673 (hull plumbed only with anchor)

findings.title: Observer-promotion correctness depends on a chain of implicit, undocumented timing invariants between TCP-direct and QUIC-relayed messages
findings.detail: The seamless ShardHandoff path only works if: (1) the client pre-opened a Secondary to the destination and it survived eviction; (2) ObserverConnect's session_token reached the destination and registered a session_observer; (3) discover_udp IP-matched the secondary's UDP src to that session_observer BEFORE promote (else udp_addr stays None and ALL post-promote PlayerInput is silently dropped — client_listener.rs:440-465 documents this exact failure); (4) the ShardPreConnect (TCP-direct system->client) and ShardHandoff (QUIC system->ship->client) arrive in a workable order — they don't, which forced the PendingSecondaryConnects buffer + per-tick retry (registry.rs:199-318) to paper over the race; (5) carrying the real planet shard_id (not placeholder 0) in ShardPreConnect so the promote key matches (ship-shard/src/main.rs:2329-2339 documents the prior placeholder-0 bug that corrupted the connection set). Each of these is an invariant enforced by comments and spawn ordering, not by types or a protocol handshake. ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (correctness by timing).

findings.title: System-shard plays dual incompatible roles (stateless relay vs stateful owner) keyed only by which optional handoff field is set
findings.detail: process_handoffs (system-shard/src/main.rs:1907-2316) branches purely on which Option in PlayerHandoff is populated: target_planet_seed -> forward to planet; target_ship_id (and !eva) -> forward to ship; target_star_index/galaxy_context -> warp arrival (spawn ship); target_system_eva -> spawn EVA player. process_handoff_accepted (2320-2486) then distinguishes locally-originated (source==self -> EVA boarding redirect) vs cross-shard relay by comparing source_shard to shard_identity. The single PlayerHandoff struct (core/src/handoff.rs:11-94) carries ~12 mutually-exclusive optional context fields for 6+ transition types; nothing enforces that the right combination is set for a given transition, so a malformed combination silently routes to the wrong branch or the 'received PlayerHandoff with no target' warn (2314). ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (one overloaded message + role multiplexing instead of typed per-transition messages).
findings.evidence: core/src/handoff.rs:11-94; system-shard/src/main.rs:1907-2316 (branch on optionals), 2333-2455 (role discrimination by source==self)

findings.title: Transfer logic embedded in 5000-9000 line monolith shard main.rs files, blocking isolation and testing
findings.detail: The transfer handlers live inside enormous Bevy app files: ship-shard/src/main.rs (~9200+ lines), system-shard/src/main.rs (~6300+ lines), planet-shard/src/main.rs (~3700+ lines). Transfer concerns are interleaved with physics, signal pipeline, terminal scrollback, HUD, autopilot, warp, colliders, etc. The handoff handlers close over dozens of resources and queries (process_handoffs on system takes 13 system params). This makes the transfer path impossible to unit-test in isolation or reason about as a unit, and is why the only tests that exist are QUIC byte round-trips. Coupling, not just size, is the problem: the spawn path is shared with the connect path via synthesized ClientConnectEvent (ship-shard:1336-1350, planet:1354-1364) so transfer and login are entangled. ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (no module boundary around transfer).
findings.evidence: ship-shard/src/main.rs (9200+ LOC), system-shard/src/main.rs (6300+ LOC), planet-shard/src/main.rs (3700+ LOC); process_handoffs signature system-shard/src/main.rs:1886-1906

findings.title: Zero tests cover the transfer state machine, observer-promotion, eviction, or any multi-shard transfer scenario
findings.detail: The only handoff tests are shard-common/tests/quic_integration.rs: send_and_receive_handoff and a 2-message ordering test — both pure QUIC serialization round-trips with observer_promoted:false. client_listener.rs internal tests (lines 1124-1157) cover only has_client/pending_udp caps; there is NO test for register_session_observer -> promote_observer_to_client, no test for discover_udp IP-matching, no test for the MAX_SECONDARIES eviction, no test for the ShardHandoff vs ShardRedirect decision, no end-to-end transfer test. core/src/character/handoff_blob.rs has round-trip tests for the character blob only. The fragile parts (promotion, eviction, ordering, failure) are entirely untested. This is why fixes regress: there is no safety net. MISSING TESTS (severity major because it is the proximate reason the user 'has hard times to fix what doesn't work').
findings.evidence: shard-common/tests/quic_integration.rs:11-152; shard-common/src/client_listener.rs:1124-1157; core/src/character/handoff_blob.rs:73-120; no e2e transfer test in e2e-tests/

findings.title: Coordinate reconstruction is duplicated across shards with hand-matched formulas and stale-clock corrections — drift bugs are structural
findings.detail: Because position must be re-expressed in each shard's local frame, the same player_local = old_rot.inverse()*(pos-old_pos) reconstruction is re-implemented independently on every receiving side: ship-shard re-entry (1263-1273), system EVA spawn (2135-2142), system EVA-boarding authoritative_spawn (2354-2366), planet ship-relative spawn (1243-1263). Each carries long comments about orbital clock skew (~110 km/s -> kilometers of error from a few ms of clock drift) and partial fixes (altitude clamp at planet:1274-1288 with ~1.8km/535m documented residual error). The handoff carries game_time + ship_system_position + ship_rotation specifically to enable these corrections, but the formula is copy-pasted, not centralized, so a fix in one path doesn't propagate. ARCHITECTURAL FLAW (no shared coordinate-transfer primitive; every transition re-derives it).

findings.title: session_observers map has no eviction or staleness sweep — only anonymous UDP observers are cleaned up
findings.detail: ClientRegistry has two observer stores: the anonymous observers Vec (UDP-only, swept by cleanup_stale_observers on a 10s OBSERVER_TIMEOUT, client_listener.rs:121-123,528-536) and session_observers HashMap (TCP-tagged, used for promotion). The session_observers map is only ever removed by promote_observer_to_client (on success) or unregister_session_observer (on explicit TCP EOF). If a secondary's TCP read loop dies without surfacing an EOF event, or the client evicts its secondary without the server noticing, the session_observers entry leaks — and worse, has_session_observer keeps returning true, so the source shard keeps choosing the seamless ShardHandoff path against a destination observer that no longer functions. The 10s timeout on the OTHER store can also prune a still-needed compositing observer if WorldState sends transiently fail. IMPLEMENTATION BUG / minor architectural gap.
findings.evidence: shard-common/src/client_listener.rs:121-123,142,338-391,528-536; promote/unregister are the only removers of session_observers

findings.title: Address resolution and QUIC sends are fire-and-forget via try_send with no delivery guarantee
findings.detail: Every inter-shard handoff message is dispatched with quic_send_tx.try_send(...) and the error is logged but never retried (e.g. system->planet forward at system-shard/src/main.rs:1917-1929, ship HandoffAccepted at ship-shard/src/main.rs:1358-1361). try_send drops the message if the channel is full. Address resolution was moved into the dispatcher with on-demand orchestrator refresh on cache miss (comments at ship-shard/src/main.rs:2648-2651), but a transient peer_registry miss (try_read fails or peer absent) silently skips the send (e.g. planet HandoffAccepted only sends 'if let Ok(reg)=try_read' at 1827, EVA forward needs find_by_type to hit). Combined with no ack-timeout, a single dropped/failed send strands the transfer permanently. IMPLEMENTATION BUG amplified by the missing-timeout architectural flaw.

findings.title: Client transition ordering relies on Bevy system-set ordering to avoid grace-ing the wrong shard — a documented near-miss
findings.detail: transition.rs:71-90 documents that latch_transitions MUST run before handle_connected/handle_secondary_connected, because when a Transitioning and a Connected event land in the same frame (the typical SHIP->EVA flow) running them in the wrong order graces the just-promoted NEW primary instead of the departed SHIP, orphaning the ship entity in source_index.by_shard and producing the 'ship disappears after EVA exit' symptom. This correctness is enforced only by configure_sets(.before(ShardRegistrySet)) (transition.rs:96-104) and the .chain() on registry systems (registry.rs:130-135). Any future system-set refactor silently reintroduces the orphan. The same file admits the PendingSecondaryConnects buffer exists solely to survive the ShardPreConnect-vs-ShardHandoff arrival race. ARCHITECTURAL FLAG (correctness via scheduler ordering of event-reactive systems).

findings.title: Salvageable: the ShardHandoff-vs-ShardRedirect decision is already centralized in one helper
findings.detail: build_post_handoff_redirect (shard-common/src/handoff_pipeline.rs:89-125) is the single source of truth for choosing seamless ShardHandoff (observer_promoted=true) vs legacy ShardRedirect, and every per-shard HandoffAccepted consumer routes through it (ship-shard:1211, planet:1841, system:2399). This is the ONE part of the transfer path with a clean single owner and is the right model to generalize. The wire protocol separation (PlayerHandoff state blob, HandoffAccepted ack with spawn_pose, character_state forward-compat blob with schema_version) is also sound and reusable. The observer-promotion CONCEPT (pre-connect as observer, promote in place for zero-RTT) is good; its IMPLEMENTATION via scattered ad-hoc maps is the problem. STRENGTH.
findings.evidence: shard-common/src/handoff_pipeline.rs:59-125; consumers at ship-shard/src/main.rs:1211, planet-shard/src/main.rs:1841, system-shard/src/main.rs:2399; core/src/handoff.rs:11-228; core/src/character/handoff_blob.rs

findings.title: EVA-boarding uses a keep-alive-until-ack pattern that the other transitions should adopt
findings.detail: Unlike ship->planet and planet->ship (which despawn on the synchronous ack and would strand on failure), the EVA->ship boarding path keeps the EVA entity alive and only despawns it in process_handoff_accepted after the destination ship acks (eva entity retained in boarding_pending, despawned at system-shard/src/main.rs:2371-2374). This is closer to a correct two-phase commit and shows the team already discovered the right shape locally — but it is applied inconsistently (only here), and still has no timeout if the ack never comes. The required 5s EvaExitCooldown hack (system-shard/src/main.rs:143-164) to stop the ship<->system<->ship 'stuck' ping-pong is direct evidence that boundary-trigger debouncing belongs in a real state machine, not per-transition cooldown components. PARTIAL STRENGTH / pattern to standardize.
findings.evidence: system-shard/src/main.rs:2348-2374 (despawn on ack), 5250-5395 (eva_boarding_detection keep-alive), 143-164 (EvaExitCooldown ping-pong hack)

summary:
The ecs-system player transfer path is a feature-first, message-reactive design with NO owner of the transfer lifecycle. A single transfer spans 4 processes (source shard, system-shard as router+owner, destination shard, client) each mutating private maps (pending_handoffs, PendingPlayerHandoffs, boarding_pending, session_observers, secondaries, GraceWindow, SpawnPoseLatch, PendingSecondaryConnects) with correctness enforced by comments, spawn ordering, and Bevy system-set ordering rather than by types, acks, or a state machine.

Lifecycle traced with evidence: (1) Triggers — ship hull_exit_check (ship->planet or ship->system EVA), planet ship-reentry & EVA boarding, warp boundary, all gated by inserting a HandoffPending marker. (2) State — one overloaded PlayerHandoff FlatBuffers table (core/src/handoff.rs:11-94, protocol/voxeldust.fbs:44) carries ~12 mutually-exclusive optional fields plus a forward-compat character blob. (3) Messaging — fire-and-forget quic_send_tx.try_send with errors only logged. (4) ShardHandoff-vs-ShardRedirect — cleanly centralized in build_post_handoff_redirect (the one well-owned piece). (5) Observer-promotion — client pre-opens secondaries, destination registers session_observers, promote_observer_to_client moves the TCP in place. (6) Destination spawn — synthesized ClientConnectEvent reuses the login spawn path. (7) Source cleanup — IMMEDIATE despawn+unregister on ack. (8/9) Failure & ship transfers — essentially unhandled.

Why it is hard to fix (root causes, in priority order): (a) HandoffPending is inserted but NEVER removed anywhere — any un-acked handoff permanently freezes the player; there is no timeout/retry/rollback in the entire codebase, and no pending map has a TTL. (b) The client secondary cap evicts an ARBITRARY (HashMap-order, not FIFO) non-scene secondary and can drop the exact secondary about to be promoted — the eviction landmine. (c) Seamless promotion correctness depends on a long chain of cross-protocol timing invariants (TCP-direct ShardPreConnect vs QUIC-relayed ShardHandoff) papered over with retry buffers and cooldown hacks. (d) Zero tests cover the state machine, promotion, eviction, or any multi-shard scenario — only QUIC byte round-trips. (e) Source despawns immediately with no ghost despite GhostUpdate/source_demote_after_ticks being defined-but-unused. (f) Coordinate reconstruction and the hull-trap depenetration are duplicated per-shard and race cross-shard sync.

Recommendation: rebuild transfer-first, keeping the multi-shard concept and the wire/blob types, but introduce a single owned transfer state machine with explicit phases, acks, timeouts, and compensating rollback.","open_questions":["Is there ANY orchestrator-side record of in-flight transfers, or is all transfer state purely in-memory across the 4 processes (implying a shard crash mid-transfer is unrecoverable)? Orchestrator redb persistence was not inspected for handoff state.","GhostUpdate is fully defined in core/handoff.rs and the fbs but appears to have zero emit sites — was the third-party-observer-continuity feature ever wired, or abandoned? Confirm no GhostUpdate sender exists.","What governs PlayerHandoff dispatch when the destination planet/ship shard is not yet provisioned (system-shard:1930-1932 just warns)? Is provisioning awaited, or is the handoff dropped, stranding HandoffPending forever?","Does the gateway/orchestrator ever reconcile a client whose primary was redirected but whose ShardRedirect was lost (no JoinResponse arrives)? No client-side redirect-ack-timeout was found.","How does galaxy<->system warp departure (the 4th transition class) initiate on the source side? warp_boundary was located but its handoff-emit path to galaxy-shard was not fully traced."],"rebuild_implications":"Rebuild transfer-first while KEEPING the multi-shard/observer-promotion CONCEPT and the existing wire types. Mandatory foundation: (1) a single explicit TransferStateMachine owned by ONE authority per transfer (most naturally the system/host shard) with named phases (Initiated -> DestPrepared/ObserverPromoted -> ClientRedirected -> SourceDrained -> Committed | Aborted), persisted enough to survive a shard crash. (2) Every phase transition gated by an explicit ack with a TTL; on timeout, a compensating rollback that removes HandoffPending and restores the source-authoritative player (the EVA keep-alive-until-ack pattern generalized). (3) Replace the overloaded PlayerHandoff optional-soup with typed per-transition messages. (4) Pin the promote-target secondary so it is exempt from MAX_SECONDARIES eviction, and make eviction真正 LRU. (5) Wire the already-designed GhostUpdate/source_demote grace so third parties never see a pop. (6) Centralize the coordinate-frame transfer into one tested primitive. (7) Build a deterministic multi-shard transfer test harness FIRST. KEEP-AND-HARDEN is not viable for the orchestration layer because the missing owner/timeout/test scaffolding is foundational, not incremental; but DO salvage handoff_pipeline.rs, the wire/blob protocol, the observer-promote registry primitives, and the client grace/compositing machinery.","salvageable":["shard-common/src/handoff_pipeline.rs — build_post_handoff_redirect is the one cleanly-owned decision point; generalize it into the new state machine's commit step","core/src/handoff.rs wire types (PlayerHandoff, HandoffAccepted, ShardHandoff, ShardRedirect, GhostUpdate, SpawnPose, ShardPreConnect) — sound protocol surface; keep but split PlayerHandoff into typed per-transition messages","core/src/character/handoff_blob.rs — versioned, forward-compatible, well-tested character state blob; reuse as-is","ClientRegistry observer primitives (register_session_observer / promote_observer_to_client / has_session_observer, discover_udp IP-matching) in shard-common/src/client_listener.rs — the promotion mechanism is correct in isolation; needs eviction/TTL and to be driven by an explicit owner","client/src/net/connection.rs unified run_connection (Primary/Secondary/Demoting modes, Promote/Demote control) — the per-connection task abstraction is good; the controller around it needs the pinning + LRU fix","client/src/shard/transition.rs + registry.rs grace/compositing machinery — dual-shard WorldState compositing and grace extrapolation are valuable; keep the mechanism but remove the implicit system-ordering correctness by giving transitions explicit phases","The observer-promotion + dual-shard compositing CONCEPT itself (pre-connect, promote-in-place, zero-RTT) — architecturally sound goal; only the scattered implementation must go","EVA keep-alive-until-ack two-phase pattern (system-shard boarding path) — the correct shape to standardize across all transitions"]}
